description: People looking at each other, eye contact and facial expressions in emotional face-to-face encounters (looked at me, smiled, hugged, head down).
Story-opening setup (pos near 0) introducing a child's school/teacher concerns and family expectations.
Clothing, outfits and physical appearance descriptions (bikinis, silver panties, baggy pants, hair, makeup).
Physical places and venues where things are seen or encountered (lobby, street, parking lot, party, New York locations).
Dogs, puppies and baby animals (finding the dog, stray dogs, adopting a baby wolf, Vixen).
Story-opening component: fires in the first few sentences of a story (pos about 0), regardless of content.
Place names and geographic locations people live in or move to (New York, Brooklyn, Montana, Los Angeles, small towns).
Crowds and groups acting collectively and noisily (everyone dancing, drumming, screaming, fans coming, friends all laughing).
Spoken numbers and quantities: heights, weights, ages, years, times and durations (five foot two, eighty one, six months).
Film and camera/photography equipment (film, FM2, lenses, fotomat, x-ray bags, negatives, photos).
Religion, faith and cultural/group identity (evangelical christians, church, official religion, gangster languages, holiday flags, family and society norms).
Sequences of physical actions by a third person, mostly a man: he stops, turns around, comes over, takes out keys, locks the door, hugs me.
Abstract reflective emotional language late in stories: grief, nostalgia, hope, intense feelings, seeing ourselves, being saved.
Lists of required tasks and procedures ('you have to' do budget, physicals, background checks, train staff, take CPR, paperwork).
Evaluative summary statements of an experience: 'it was a pretty amazing thing', 'a very scary/traumatic/difficult time', 'greatest moment'.
Shared relationship and closeness using 'we': we were close, we talked, we loved each other, we met in college, felt like brothers.
First-person searching, sifting and looking around (looking for an eye, digging through a box, wandering in a daze, looking up).
Therapy, counseling and self-help groups (therapy, men's work, group of therapists, minister, scream therapy, support classes).
Food and drink items and meals (pasta, red wine, sausages, french fries, yellow rice, pancakes, waffles, cube steaks).
Oregon Trail wagon-train scenario: wagons, supplies, sick travelers, hardships (weather, hunger, wild animals), farmers and gold miners.
Letters, documents and written objects (letter, envelope, stamp, cover letter, paragraph, scroll with writing, form, cards).
Rapid-speech component: fires on TRs with 13+ syllables, typically fast 'i was like / they were like' reported dialogue.
First-person travel and locomotion from place to place (got in a cab and went home, drove back, ran upstairs, headed over the border).
References to family members and personal relations (my mom, my sister, my boyfriend, my son, great grandmother, friend's parents).
Forceful physical body actions and struggle (swing, headlock, push him backwards, drop the bra, hold with feet, neck snapped, blood fell).
Introspective first-person feeling/thinking statements: i didn't know how i felt, i felt betrayed, i knew he was right, i thought, i cried.
Navy water-survival/parachute training procedures: canopy, release from the boat, three-line jettison, checklist, raft, horizon.
Spatial descriptions of rooms and built locations (lobby, deck on the side of the trailer, parking lot, windowless chamber, stairs, stage).
Describing plural groups or categories of people (friends who are all writers, swedish and german girls, irish catholics, freaks, farmers and gold miners).
Mostly the repeated shouted command 'pick up the gun'; also pay-phone coin mechanics and music references - no unified concept.
Silence-firing component: fires on empty/pause TRs (spr=0) during narrative beats.
Quotative 'i was like / he was like' reported dialogue and reactions.
Medical procedures and hospital treatment (surgery, emergency room, IV, scans, blood work, transfusions, liver transplant, stitches).
Foreign-language phrases, unusual words and proper names (la botella de agua, aidez moi, acedia, seguin, san antonio, que somme fait plaisir).
Biographical career/education milestones (graduated college, started modeling, quit my job and started consulting, sophomore at princeton, moved to new york).
Religious and funeral ritual actions (shamanistic objects, prayers, flowers, ringing the bell, ashes to the river, incense, walking around the coffin).
Narrator framing and transition phrases ('the biggest thing that happened', 'at this point in the story', 'the worst part was', 'about a year ago').
Urgent fast-paced first-person movement sequences (we got to go, i jump out and run in, i went out and walked over, ran to the freezer).
Unusual tokens: proper names, foreign words, onomatopoeia and spelled-out letters (ra ra ra, le bernadin, susan orlean, s o f i a, vato loco).
Describing a person's personality and character traits (nerdy virgin, brilliant and entertaining, strong silent type, well liked, energetic and fun).
States of physical or emotional suffering (headache, hung over, depressed can't get out of bed, really down, in shock, panic, numb).
First-person self-reflective statements about own tendencies and feelings, often with hesitant repetition ('i tend to', 'i can't help but', 'i could never understand').
Habitual or hypothetical 'you would / we would' procedural narration (you'd march it out and set it down, we would talk, i'd drop my bra and run).
Casual vernacular quoted dialogue with 'he's like / i'm like', especially the football-catching exchange (you still wanna play football, momma's boy).
Quoted questions, requests and instructions in dialogue (what did he say, what's wrong with you, tell me about it, fill it out and bring it back, asked him if).
Natural landscape and scenery descriptions (hills, mountains and ocean, cliffs, canyon, dry lakes, desert, river banks, temples across the river).
Quoted speech directly addressing 'you' with propositions, questions or commands (i'll put you in a video if you'll give me, take the form to the desk, if you get a tattoo).
Silence-firing component: fires on empty/pause TRs (spr=0), e.g. comedic beats and story endings.
Rapid-speech component: fires on TRs with 13+ syllables of fast dense speech regardless of topic.
Silence-firing component: fires on empty/pause TRs (spr=0) at punchlines and section breaks.
